title: The Pencil Nebula, a strangely shaped leftover from a vast explosion
caption: The Pencil Nebula, NGC 2736, imaged by the MPG/ESO 2.2-meter telescope at La Silla
celestial: NGC 2736 · constellation Vela · about 800 light-years away (source figure)

recognition.text: Ranked #85 on ESO’s published “Top 100 Images” list (an institutional selection, not an audience score).

story: This picture shows the oddly shaped Pencil Nebula, cataloged as NGC 2736. The camera responsible is the Wide Field Imager, mounted on the MPG/ESO 2.2-meter telescope at ESO's La Silla site in Chile.

The Pencil is a small piece of a much larger remnant left behind after a supernova, the explosion of a star, which took place about 11 000 years ago. When a massive star explodes, it flings its material outward at high speed, and as that debris plows into the thin gas between the stars it compresses and heats it, making it glow.

The image was recorded through several broad color filters and one that isolates the red glow of hydrogen, which highlights the heated gas. The official caption offers few further details about the nebula.
scale: Using the source's listed field of view (33.16 x 33.16 arcminutes) and distance (800 light years), the frame spans roughly 7.7 × 7.7 light-years. Its light set out about 800 years before reaching the telescope.

understand.summary: This visible-light image from the Wide Field Imager combines B, V and R filters with a hydrogen filter. The source does not publish which color was assigned to each filter.
understand.eye: Long exposures gather far more light than the eye, so this faint glowing filament would not look like this by eye.

behind.exposure: Not published on the source page.
behind.technique: Not stated by the source (single frame, stack, mosaic or panorama unknown).

alt: The oddly shaped Pencil Nebula, a small part of a supernova remnant.
